items.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: I never have known what happened to this guy, I remember his name, he was on late every night out of Frankfurt, his name was Joe Neidig.

ctx.x: What was the music like that you heard as a youth? Do you remember specific —

Oh I remember a great deal of it because I was born in 1936, so by the time I was becoming conscious of music the war was just over, but the American Forces Network was going strong in Europe, and so I tuned in — the radio was THE thing. I lived for the radio, because that’s of course where I first heard jazz. And there was quite a bit of it on BBC, played of course by local bands, some of which were pretty good. But I had the huge advantage of being able to tune in the American Forces Network. And there was, in…
This man was a D.J., not a band leader.

Yeah. No he was a D.J. It was amazing because a daunting sort of task he must have had every day, because he would have conversations between the record that he played, he’d maybe play a conversation out of a radio drama, it might be “The Whistler,” and he would have a conversation with tape. It must have taken him all day, because in those days it was slicing with a razor blade, right, to edit tape. It was great, it was great, it was a lot of fun.
